title: Mandiri Jogja Marathon 2027 Review: What the 2026 Race Was Like
seo_title: Mandiri Jogja Marathon Review: Prambanan Course, Heat, Cut-offs
meta_description: Mandiri Jogja Marathon review from the 2026 race: a temple course around Prambanan, 23°C at the 4.45am start, 21 water stations, a seven-hour limit and how fast 6,193 timed finishers ran.
dek: What Indonesia's temple marathon was like in 2026: the course past Prambanan and Plaosan, cool air at the start and full sun by the finish, the aid and cut-offs, and how quickly the field actually ran.
verdict: Enter if you want a big, well-supplied marathon with a seven-hour limit and a genuinely different backdrop. The 2026 race drew a record 10,200 runners from 17 countries to a course that starts and finishes at Prambanan and passes four more temples and several villages, with water every 2 to 3 km. The air at the 4.45am start was a mild 23°C, but skies were clear, and by the time half the marathon field finished, after 5:14, it had passed 27°C in sunshine. The front is fast, with Kenyan winners under 2:21, while the middle is relaxed: only one marathoner in ten broke four hours.

sections.heading: The Course: Five Temples and the Villages Between
paragraphs: All four races start and finish in the Prambanan temple area on the border of Sleman and Central Java [3][8]. The marathon was flagged off at the temple itself at 4.45am [3]. From there the route passed the Sewu, Lumbung and Bubrah temples inside the park, then Plaosan temple, the Taruna monument and a string of traditional villages before returning to Prambanan [4][5]. The roads are asphalt, and the organiser placed gamelan players, marching bands and choirs at cheering points along the way [6].

The course is AIMS-certified [4][8]. The official route page carries only map images and GPX downloads, with no written description or elevation profile [1]. The 2026 theme was the Sumbu Filosofis, Yogyakarta's UNESCO-listed Philosophical Axis, but that link was carried by the finisher medal, a Panggung Krapyak design that is the second of a five-medal series running to 2029, not by the route, which stays in the Prambanan area [6].

Road quality has been the long-running complaint. A runner who reviewed the 2024 marathon described a long climb to about 26 km, a steep descent from 28 to 30 km, patched roads with potholes, narrow cambered lanes and a long stretch shared with the half marathon [14]. The published 2026 maps do not show whether those sections were still on the course, so check the GPX before race day.

sections.heading: The Weather: Cool at the Start, Clear and Hot by the Finish
paragraphs: Open-Meteo's reanalysis for the grid point nearest Prambanan shows about 23°C, a 22°C dew point and 95% humidity at the 4.45am start, with almost no wind and a clear sky [16]. It cooled slightly to 22°C at 6am, then warmed fast once the sun was up: 24°C at 7am, 26°C at 8am, 28°C at 9am and 30°C by 11am, still under a cloudless sky [16].

That makes this a race of two halves. A three-and-a-half-hour marathoner finished at about 8.15am in air that was still bearable; the median marathoner, finishing after 5:14, came home at about 10am, at 29°C in full sun. The winner of the national masters marathon said the sun was quite fierce on the day [6]. Bank early, and use the cooling stations in the second half.

sections.heading: Aid Stations and Cut-offs
paragraphs: The rules promise water every 2 to 3 km and at the finish [2]. In 2026 the marathon had 21 water stations, more than before, according to the organiser's partners, with giant fans and cooling sponges on the course and a cooling-spray cheering point [6][7].

The cut-offs were seven hours for the marathon (11.45am), four hours for the half (9.15am), two hours for the 10 km (8am) and one hour for the 5 km (7.15am) [1]. The rules also allow intermediate time limits at points announced before the race; finishing outside the limit means a DNF with no medal [2]. The cut-offs bit lightly: the slowest timed half marathoner finished in 3:56, inside the limit, and six marathon times are listed beyond seven hours [17]. Marathon and half-marathon finishers get a finisher tee as well as the medal [1].

sections.heading: Roads, Safety and Marshalling
paragraphs: Course security is run by the local police and transport office, and the organiser provides medical cover with local hospitals [2]. Every entrant except under-18s in the 5 km was covered by personal-accident insurance [1]. No death or serious medical incident was reported at the 2026 race.

Marshals enforced the bib rule. A video that went viral on race day showed staff removing a runner without a bib from the course while a registered runner argued that the man was with him; reports differ on whether it happened mid-route or near the finish, and online reaction largely backed the officers [10][11]. Unregistered runners should expect to be pulled out.

sections.heading: How Fast the Field Is
paragraphs: The front of the race is international. The open marathon was won in 2:20:28 by a Kenyan man and 2:39:35 by a Kenyan woman, and the half marathon in 1:03:31 and 1:16:51; the 10 km went in 30:38 and 35:16 [8][9]. The fastest Indonesian man in the national marathon category ran about 2:30 [8][9].

Behind the front, the field is broad and recreational. The marathon had 994 timed finishers: tenth place was 2:34:57, the median 5:14:32 and the slowest tenth took more than 6:33. Only 10% broke four hours and 43% broke five, and 15% of finishers were women [17]. The half marathon had 2,545 finishers with a median of 2:40:16; only 8.5% broke two hours and 37% broke 2:30, and 30% were women. The 10 km had 2,654 finishers, a median of 1:22:20 and 43% women [17].

Prize money is deep. The open marathon pays Rp120 million to the winners, and the national-only and masters marathon categories each pay five places, from Rp100 million down to Rp20 million, identical for men and women [12]. Tenth woman in the marathon ran 3:33:25 [17], so the masters and national women's places are within reach of a strong club runner.

sections.heading: Race Weekend Logistics
paragraphs: Race packs were collected from 18 to 20 June, 10am to 8pm, at the Yogyakarta Marriott on the northern ring road, with the confirmation and the ID used to register; a representative could collect with a signed authorisation [13]. Runners gathered at the start from 4am, and the marathon flag-off followed a parade of palace soldiers at 4.15am [3].

Fees in 2026 were Rp1,200,000 for the open marathon, Rp900,000 for the half, Rp800,000 for the 10 km and Rp450,000 for the 5 km, with cheaper national categories [1]. Bibs cannot be transferred and fees are not refunded [2]. The race village at Prambanan had a local-brands market and stage [4][5].

sections.heading: Should You Enter the 2027 Race?
paragraphs: Yes, if you want a big, certified marathon with real prize money, generous water and a seven-hour limit: in 2026 half the marathon field finished after 5:14 and almost nobody was cut. The temple setting and the village crowds make it one of the most distinctive road races in the region.

Think twice if you want a fast time without the heat. The start is cool, but clear June mornings mean full sun from about 7am, and past editions had rough road surfaces and a hilly section after halfway.
The AIMS calendar lists the 2027 race for Sunday 20 June [15]; the organiser had not confirmed it when this was written.
Nobody from this site ran the race. This review draws on the organiser's race information, the full results, modelled weather data, Indonesian press reports and a runner's account of the 2024 race.

faqs.question: What time does the Mandiri Jogja Marathon start?
faqs.answer: In 2026 the marathon started at 4.45am at Prambanan temple, the half marathon at 5.15am, the 10 km at 6am and the 5 km in two waves at 6.15am and 6.20am. Runners gathered from 4am. Times for the 20 June 2027 race had not been published when this was written.

faqs.question: How hot is the Mandiri Jogja Marathon?
faqs.answer: Mild at the start, hot by the finish. Modelled weather for the Prambanan area shows about 23°C and 95% humidity at the 4.45am start in 2026, under a clear sky. It reached 26°C by 8am, 28°C by 9am and 30°C by 11am, so slower marathoners finish in full sun.

faqs.question: How fast do you need to be to place at the Mandiri Jogja Marathon?
faqs.answer: Very fast in the open race: Kenyan runners won the 2026 marathon in 2:20:28 and 2:39:35, and tenth overall was 2:34:57. The national and masters categories pay five places each, from Rp100 million down to Rp20 million, and tenth woman overall ran 3:33:25.

faqs.question: How many people finish the Mandiri Jogja Marathon?
faqs.answer: In 2026, 994 runners finished the marathon, 2,545 the half marathon and 2,654 the 10 km, out of a record 10,200 entrants across four races. Half the marathon finishers took longer than 5:14, and only one in ten broke four hours, so a slow finish puts you in good company.

editorial_notes: Written 2026-11-06 about the previous edition (Sunday 21 June 2026), for runners deciding on the 2027 race. Finish-time figures are Run SEA's analysis of the official Sada Raga results (timing junk filtered; none found); whether the times are gun or chip is not stated. Weather is Open-Meteo modelled reanalysis for the grid point nearest Prambanan, not a station observation: Adisucipto airport had no archived METAR for the morning and Yogyakarta International is about 50 km away on the coast. The route page gives maps only, so the course is described from the landmarks named in press reports; the Sumbu Filosofis theme belongs to the medal series, not the route, contrary to earlier research notes. Intermediate cut-off points were promised but not found. Course-surface detail is from a 2024 runner's review and is labelled as such. The bib dispute is reported without names; reports disagree on where it happened. A 2025 death reported in search snippets was not verified and is not mentioned. No rating.
